messages:
jia: heads up — QA found a repro where the console preview pane shows another org's dataset when you quick-preview a saved search. steps:
1) open org-A, saved search list
2) hover preview on item that references a run from org-B
3) preview pane loads org-B rows

jia: looks like the preview prefetch call doesn't include the tenant header, so the backend falls back to resource-scoped resolution and returns the wrong rows. attaching a small curl i used to repro:

jia: ```http
GET /internal/preview?search_id=sn-1234 HTTP/1.1
Host: console-internal
Cookie: session=xxxx
# note: no X-Workspace or X-Tenant header
``` 

oscar: oh no. is this limited to prefetch/preview or do other client-side routes do the same? :eyes:

jia: I only checked preview and the quicklink hover handler. the normal saved-search detail load sends the tenant header correctly (we pass workspaceId in route), so this was a subtle missing header in the hover prefetch path.

anita: thanks for the repro. can you paste the backend log trace for the request? i want to see which auth middleware branch handled it.

jia: pasted the minimal log lines:

jia: ```
INFO 2065432100 RequestId=abc123 path=/internal/preview auth=anonymous resolved_resource=search:sn-1234 owner_org=org-b
INFO 2065432101 PermissionCheck fallback_to_resource_scope=true
``` 

sam: ugh. likely cause: the hover prefetch is made from a service worker fetch that strips custom headers in the fetch() call because we used credentials: 'omit' earlier when fixing cookie flash. good candidate for regression from the prefetch refactor.

lauren: if it is the service-worker fetch, we need to be careful — adding tenant headers into client side code might leak to third-party hosts if we ever change preview to use absolute urls. prefer fixing by ensuring server resolves using session->workspace mapping when cookie present rather than falling back to resource-scope resolution.

oscar: +1 to server-side defense. we should never resolve to a different org just because header was missing. fall back must check session workspace and deny cross-org resource access.

anita: agree. short plan:
- patch preview handler to require tenant header OR validate session workspace before resolving (server change) — HIGH
- update hover prefetch to include headers/credentials (frontend) — MED
- add unit/integration test for preview prefetch path (e2e) — MED

anita: i'll open a PR for the server check now, can someone own the frontend change? sam?

sam: I can do the frontend fix — will include a test for service worker fetch options and ensure credentials:'include' so cookies + session are present. will also add guard to avoid putting headers on absolute external urls.

lauren: deploy-bot will run after PR merge — remember to include a migration note for the security changelog. even if it's internal, call it out in the SRE incident channel if a rollback is needed.

deploy-bot: CI passed, staging deploy queued — keep me posted on canary metrics (preview latency/404s) :rocket:

jia: thanks all. repro steps + logs are in a gist I shared in #eng-platform earlier. i'll reply here once server PR is up.

anita: once server PR is merged, let's run a quick org-to-org preview smoke test across 3 workspaces. also add a telemetry event for when preview falls back to resource-scope so we can detect any remaining exposures.

oscar: small follow-up: add a linter rule to flag fetch() usage without credentials explicitly set where we expect cookies. saved us before.

sam: noted. making it part of my frontend PR.

jia: update — server PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pull/4873 , patch adds session validation and an audit log entry when fallback happened. PTAL.

anita: reviewing now.

lauren: thanks team. recorded follow-up in #eng-sre for telemetry dashboards. will watch for any spike in preview fallback events after the fix.
